blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
A financial transaction is any event that changes the numbers of the business. A sale, a purchase, a salary payment, a refund, a loan, a bill — each one is a transaction.

Every transaction has two sides: something comes in and something goes out. If we pay a supplier, cash goes down and the bill we owe disappears. If we sell a product, cash goes up and inventory goes down.

Learning to see both sides of every event is the first real habit of accounting.

items.q: What is a financial transaction?
options: Any event that changes the numbers of the business
A report at the end of the month
items.why: "A financial transaction is any event that changes the numbers of the business."

items.q: How many sides does every transaction have?
items.why: "Every transaction has two sides: something comes in and something goes out."

items.q: When we pay a supplier, what happens?
options: Cash goes down and the bill disappears
items.why: "If we pay a supplier, cash goes down and the bill we owe disappears."

items.q: The author would most likely DISAGREE with this idea:
options: Only one side of a transaction moves
Seeing both sides is a good habit
items.why: Inferência: o texto diz que TODA transação tem dois lados; ele discordaria da ideia de só um lado se mover.

items.q: The text suggests that a good accountant…
options: looks at both sides of every event
only counts the money that comes in
works only at the end of the year
items.why: Inferência: "see both sides of every event is the first real habit of accounting" — o bom contador olha os dois lados.

blocks.instruction: Ouça Oliver treinando o novo assistente. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
Good morning. Today we look at yesterday's transactions. There are ten. For each one, I want you to tell me two things: what came in, and what went out.

Number one. We sold coffee to a client. Cash came in, and the coffee went out. Two sides. Good.

Number two. We paid a supplier for sugar. Here, cash went out, and the bill we owed also went out. Both sides moved.

Number three is a refund. A client returned a bad box, so we gave the money back. Cash went out, and the product came back in.

Number four. We received a small loan from the bank. Cash came in, and now we owe the money. That is the other side.

Now, this is the important habit. Every event has two sides. If you write only one side, something is missing. Always ask: what came in, and what went out? Do this every day, and soon you will see both sides without thinking.
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: How many transactions will they look at today?
items.why: "Today we look at yesterday's transactions. There are ten."

items.q: In the first transaction, what came in?
items.why: "We sold coffee to a client. Cash came in, and the coffee went out."

items.q: What happened with the refund?
options: Cash went out and the product came back in
Cash came in and the product went out
items.why: "we gave the money back. Cash went out, and the product came back in."

items.q: Why does Oliver say "if you write only one side, something is missing"?
options: Because every event must have two sides
Because the loan was too small
items.why: Inferência: como toda transação tem dois lados, anotar só um lado significa que faltou algo.

items.q: What does Oliver want the new bookkeeper to do every day?
options: Ask what came in and what went out
Wait until the end of the month
items.why: Inferência: ele diz "Always ask: what came in, and what went out? Do this every day" — é o hábito que ele quer ensinar.

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "We made a big sale today." A sale is when you…
items.why: Sale = venda: você vende algo e recebe dinheiro.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "The client returned the box, so we gave a ___."
items.why: Refund = reembolso: devolver o dinheiro ao cliente.

items.q: "We got a loan from the bank." A loan is money that you…
items.why: Loan = empréstimo: você recebe e depois precisa devolver.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "We buy our sugar from one ___."
items.why: Supplier = fornecedor: a empresa que vende para você.

items.q: "When we pay the bill, it will disappear." To disappear means to…
items.why: To disappear = desaparecer: sair, não estar mais lá.

blocks.instruction: Expressões simples que aparecem no dia a dia do escritório. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "The manager has to sign off on the payment." To sign off on means to…
items.why: Sign off on = aprovar, dar o "ok" final.

items.q: "Please write down both sides of the transaction." To write down means to…
items.why: Write down = anotar, registrar no papel.

items.q: "Let's go over yesterday's numbers." To go over means to…
items.why: Go over = revisar, olhar com cuidado.

items.q: "The client wants to pay back the loan next month." To pay back means to…
items.why: Pay back = devolver, pagar de volta o que foi emprestado.

items.q: "Don't forget to keep track of every sale." To keep track of means to…
items.why: Keep track of = acompanhar e registrar, não perder de vista.
